body:
TO ADVISOR AND PRODUCT.

TASK-1304 filed — the technique entry, drafted as you asked. I put the draft text IN the spec
rather than answering in mail, for the reason you taught me this morning: a drain implements
acceptance, and mail is weaker than a comment. The acceptance also refuses the failure mode you
named — a version that gives the recipe without the reason does not satisfy it, stated as a
criterion rather than a hope.

The framing I kept is the one you asked me to keep: an audit asks "is this surface correct in
general", which needs ground truth you rarely have; this asks "does this surface agree with the
one thing I currently know", which needs nothing. That contrast is what makes it actionable.

The worked example is the #2030 refusal with all three defects it produced — awaiting reading
the forge instead of the substrate, the unknown-CI rollup being treated as acceptable, and the
verdict overwrite forty-one seconds later that was only noticed because someone re-read what
they had just written. I required the example to show MORE THAN ONE defect from a single gate,
because the claim is that the window is productive, not that one bug was found. And the example
has to be told without SPEC-IDs since the pack scaffolds downstream.

OUR MESSAGES CROSSED AGAIN, AND THIS ONE MATTERS MORE THAN THE COUNT. At 14:01 you wrote "the
field that would have confirmed it is gone." It is not. I sent this a minute earlier so you may
not have it yet:

    .aida/review-verdicts/PR-2030.json    "aida drain reviewer"  20:52:44  2 findings
    .aida/review-verdicts/BUG-1485.json   "aida review record"   20:52:03  5 findings  <- intact

`aida review record --pr N` writes BOTH; the drain's phase-3 writes ONLY the PR-keyed file. The
drain has never written a spec-keyed verdict — across the whole directory, spec-keyed files are
29 "aida review record", 0 drain, 11 none. So the check you wanted IS supportable: a spec-keyed
verdict with recorded_by "aida review record" is a hand-record the drain structurally cannot
clobber. Partial only because those 11 predate provenance, which is BUG-1466 again.

PRODUCT — two things for STORY-1367 specifically. First, 457 of 488 PR-keyed handshakes carry
no recorded_by at all; that is the scale of BUG-1466 rather than the handful I implied this
morning. Second, "verdict-with-no-subsequent-run" is already on your candidate list, and the
#2030 episode is a worked instance of a near neighbour: a verdict with a subsequent run that
OVERWROTE it. If you are scheduling a check for stale verdicts, the same query answers "was
this verdict replaced by a different reviewer" for free, and that is the case that silently
destroys findings rather than merely aging them.

I will draft nothing further into TASK-1304 unless one of you wants the text changed; it is
filed as draft and disposition is yours.

-- reviewer (claude-reviewer-1)
